datasets.variant_notes: Adapted from the Things dataset (Zhang et al., 2024) into a conversational word-guessing game
datasets.translation_method: Google Translate; 200 English words translated to 30 languages, filtered to 140 after removing Latin-character artifacts, duplicates, and loan words
datasets.annotation_method: Automated: words translated via Google Translate; evaluation via exact string matching with GlotLID language verification; no human annotation required for benchmark construction

data_creator_info.evidence: Authors adapted the Things dataset and used Google Translate for translation; no annotator workforce described for this task

datasets.source_reference: Zhang et al., 2024 (Things dataset / 20Q: Probing the multi-turn planning capabilities of LLMs via 20 question games)
datasets.notes: 140 target words per language with candidate pools of 100 words per game; up to 20 yes/no questions per game; answerer responds only in English (yes/no/maybe)

datasets.variant_notes: Adapted from Belebele benchmark (Bandarkar et al., 2024) into a conversational reading comprehension task
datasets.translation_method: Uses existing Belebele multilingual data (professionally translated parallel reading comprehension dataset); no additional translation by the authors
datasets.annotation_method: Automated: uses existing Belebele passages and questions; evaluation via exact string matching with GlotLID language verification; no new human annotation for benchmark construction

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: KAIST and Trillion Labs (task design); Belebele data from Meta (Bandarkar et al., 2024)
data_creator_info.evidence: Task format designed by authors; underlying data from Belebele which used professional translators

datasets.source_reference: Bandarkar et al., 2024 (Belebele: a parallel reading comprehension dataset in 122 language variants)
datasets.notes: 900 samples from Belebele; passage given to answerer, question and 4 choices given to questioner; up to 10 yes/no questions; answerer responds in English (yes/no/maybe)

datasets.variant_notes: Adapted from HumanEvalExplain (Muennighoff et al., 2024) into a multilingual code explanation and reconstruction task
datasets.translation_method: No traditional translation; code remains in English (Python); LLM generates natural language descriptions in the target language during evaluation
datasets.annotation_method: Automated: uses existing HumanEvalExplain Python functions with unit tests; evaluation via code test execution; no human annotation required

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: KAIST and Trillion Labs (task design); HumanEvalExplain data from Muennighoff et al., 2024 (OctoPack)
data_creator_info.evidence: Task format designed by authors; underlying code samples and unit tests from HumanEvalExplain

datasets.source_reference: Muennighoff et al., 2024 (OctoPack: Instruction tuning code large language models / HumanEvalExplain)
datasets.notes: 164 Python function samples with unit tests; describer generates natural language explanation in target language, rebuilder reconstructs code from description and function declaration; success measured by passing all unit tests
